The newly emerged hatchling weighs just 2.4 grams [Ww0 = 2.4 grams], a tiny initial mass that underscores the altricial state of the neonate, which is entirely dependent on biparental provisioning for its early development. The chick's featherless, helpless condition at emergence stands in stark contrast to the active, moss-gleaning adult that will eventually attain a much larger body size after many weeks of rapid growth within the nest.

Puberty, defined here as the onset of gonadal activity and the completion of somatic growth, is attained at 42 days after hatching [tp = 42 days after hatching] under the same thermal conditions of 40.2 °C [T = 40.2 °C], a comparatively rapid maturation compared to some larger Andean passerines.
